hints: Compare coefficients of $x^2$ and the constant term with $6x^2 - 21$.
walkthrough:
Form the composite function $fg(x)$ by substituting $g(x) = ax^2 + b$ into $f(x) = 2x + 3$:
$$fg(x) = 2(ax^2 + b) + 3 = 2ax^2 + 2b + 3$$

Equate coefficients with the given formula $fg(x) = 6x^2 - 21$:
$$2a = 6 \implies a = 3$$
$$2b + 3 = -21$$

hints: Note that the domain of $f$ is $x \ge 0$, so $g(x) \ge 0$ is required for $fg(x)$ to exist.
Since $x \le q$, deduce the maximum value $q = -2$.
walkthrough:
Recall that the composite function $fg(x)$ is defined only when the range of $g$ lies within the domain of $f$ ($x \ge 0$):
$$g(x) \ge 0 \implies 3x^2 - 12 \ge 0$$

Solve the quadratic inequality for $x$:
$$3x^2 \ge 12 \implies x^2 \ge 4 \implies x \le -2 \quad\text{or}\quad x \ge 2$$

Since the domain of $g$ is given by $x \le q$, all values of $x \le q$ must satisfy $x \le -2$:
$$q \le -2 \implies \text{Greatest possible value of } q \text{ is } -2$$

hints: Note that $x^2$ increases as $x \le -3$ moves further negative.
walkthrough:
State the range of $fg$, noting that as $x \to -\infty$, $fg(x) \to \infty$:
$$\text{Range: } y \ge 33 \quad (\text{or } fg(x) \ge 33)$$

hints: Choose the negative square root since the domain is $x \le -3$.
The domain of $(fg)^{-1}$ is the range of $fg$ found in part (iii).
walkthrough:
Set $y = 6x^2 - 21$ and rearrange to isolate $x^2$:
$$6x^2 = y + 21 \implies x^2 = \frac{y + 21}{6}$$

Take the square root, choosing the negative branch because the domain is $x \le -3$:
$$x = -\sqrt{\frac{y + 21}{6}}$$

Write the inverse function in terms of $x$:
$$(fg)^{-1}(x) = -\sqrt{\frac{x + 21}{6}}$$

State the domain of $(fg)^{-1}(x)$, which equals the range of $fg(x)$ from part (iii):
$$\text{Domain: } x \ge 33$$
